Subject: CAIQ mapping request — tenant isolation and GPU tenancy for inference

Hi Mina,

We're doing a CAIQ deep-dive for Nebula Health and a couple of controls came up that our auditors want tied specifically to inference runtime behavior: KV-cache/ prefix caching isolation (to make sure customers' prompt state can't leak), GPU tenancy/hypervisor isolation guarantees for dedicated pools, and evidence that ephemeral logs don't contain PII in the inference trace.

Can you provide a mapping (control ID -> Redwood evidence/artifact) that covers: CCM-DataIsolation (tenant boundary), CCM-ComputeIsolation (GPU tenancy), and CCM-Logging (ephemeral trace redaction)? Ideally we'd like a short narrative, the authoritative artifact (runbook/arch diagram), and one or two log snippets showing redaction/obfuscation.

Timeline: our audit window opens 2026-03-08 — can you confirm if Redwood can deliver a mapping + sample artifacts by 2026-02-26?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call if that's easier.

Alyssa Turner
Director, Security & Compliance
Nebula Health
security@nebulahealth.com

  2) Evidence bundle: architecture diagram (tenant isolation), runtime runbook excerpt (how KV cache keys are segregated), a sanitized runtime log snippet demonstrating redaction, and an evidence manifest PDF.
  3) A short tech note explaining how our smart routing + fallback preserves isolation guarantees across Dedicated and Private modes.

- Owners: Marissa will assemble the evidence pack and legal-safe artifact; David will pull the runtime logs and produce the sanitized snippets; I'll review and add the CAIQ narratives.

I've attached a working spreadsheet (rdw-caiq-kv-gpu-mapping-draft.xlsx) with the initial mapping columns (Control ID, Redwood assertion, Evidence file, Owner, Notes). Marissa / Mina / Alyssa — sending the first pass artifacts and short notes. Attached: rdw-runtime-log-sample.txt (sanitized), rdw-evidence-manifest.pdf. Also updated the spreadsheet mapping with the evidence filenames.

Key notes (short):
- KV-cache isolation: our runtime prefixes cache keys with tenant-id + region-hash. Sample below (sanitized):

  [2026-02-23T09:12:31Z] INFER TRACE tenant=nebula-123 op=prefix-set key=tenant_nebula-123::sess_8f3a... action=kv_set size=128
  [2026-02-23T09:12:33Z] INFER TRACE tenant=nebula-123 op=kv-get key=tenant_nebula-123::sess_8f3a... hit=true latency_ms=12

  Note: keys are deterministic prefixes and do not contain raw prompt text. The log scrubber strips prompt payloads before persistence — see rdw-runtime-log-sample.txt and the redaction section in the manifest.

- GPU tenancy / Dedicated pools: Dedicated capacity is provisioned as tenant-bound pools (no co-tenancy). The compute allocator marks allocation records with node_tenancy=dedicated and tenant_id=<tenant>. For private/on-prem installs we include an explicit caveat in the CAIQ: customer-managed tenancy may vary and we document the recommended configuration for the on-prem package.

- Limitations / caveats: 
  * Private deployments: CAIQ narrative will show the expected config and point to the deployment checklist; evidence will be a guidance artifact rather than runtime logs if the customer is in an air-gapped environment.
  * Shared/hosted: we can produce live runtime allocation audit for the audit window (date-stamped).

Next steps: Marissa — please confirm when you upload the final zip to the shared Drive link and I'll send the formal CAIQ crosswalk (control ID -> assertion -> artifact) to Alyssa.

Thanks,
David Kim
Principal Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
